forward_patch:

@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M8488WPHV0RC4W665XDRV99B
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: 8b80
+title: 'Inkling 2 decode: spread the depth mix and the other single-row kernels over the GPU'
+---
+## Why
+The ^pxcccjs attribution: with attention, MoE and lm_head all skipped, a decode step still costs 2.9 ms/token while moving almost no bytes. That remainder is the depth mix (×2 per visit), the message controllers (24 visits) and the convolution states. `inkling2DepthMix` puts one row in one threadgroup, so a decode step (1 row) runs it on a single threadgroup, twice in each of the 48 visits.
+
+## What
+- Sub-attribute the 2.9 ms between depth mix, message controllers and the rest, with skips as in scratchpad/ablation.patch.
+- Split the depth mix of one row across threadgroups: by block or by channel slice, then a small reduce. Or fold the MLP depth mix into the router logits kernel, which reads its float32 copy.
+
+## Acceptance
+- [ ] inklingcheck.sh: CHECK PASS.
+- [ ] inklingbench.sh shows a decode gain beyond the noise.
+- [ ] The bf16 decode kernel tests pass. #inkling-perf
\ No newline at end of file

@@ -1,6 +1,19 @@

 assignees:
 - claude-code
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m84r1vpdshgnpmt31k7edmp7
+  text: |-
+    ## Measured, dropped: the depth mix costs ≤ ~1 ms of GPU per token, behind a host-bound decode
+    - Microbenchmark: 96 calls of `inkling2DepthMix`, one decode step's worth (2 per visit), one row, D=2304, independent, in one eval. Through a temporary public hook, since removed.
+      - K=4 Q=1 conv: 0.87 ms (9.1 us each)
+      - K=8 Q=1 conv: 1.17 ms (12.2 us)
+      - K=4 Q=3: 1.11 ms (11.6 us)
+      - K=8 Q=3: 1.16 ms (12.1 us)
+    - Spreading one row across threadgroups needs a second reduce kernel, so 96 more dispatches per token. After ^jddp2ck decode is still host-bound: the GPU is busy ~83%, and each dispatch costs ~16 us of encode. The best case is ~0.5 ms of GPU time saved, behind the host, for more host work. A net loss is likely, so the card is dropped.
+    - If decode becomes GPU-bound later, e.g. after an upstream MLX encode speedup, the better move is to fold the MLP-input depth mix into the router-logits pass rather than add a reduce kernel.
+  timestamp: 2026-11-23T17:42:54.413280+00:00
 depends_on:
 - 01M8488WPHV0RC4W665XDRV99B
 position_column: doing
